briefing.text: DATA STRUCTURE (read from file headers only; no analysis has been done and nothing below has been counted). The h5ad for this task (local file 158542059.node; the library saw it at /scbench-data/158542059.node, so use whatever path you are given) has 100,000 cells x 40,352 genes. The var index holds gene symbols. X is a sparse matrix of raw integer counts; there are no layers and no uns. obs columns include: donor (Donor1..Donor12), cytokine (91 levels, including the exact labels 'IFN-beta' and 'PBS'), treatment (only two levels, 'PBS' vs 'cytokine'), cell_type (18 levels, including the exact label 'CD14 Mono') and sample (1092 levels = donor_cytokine). Because the 100k cells are spread over 1092 donor x cytokine samples and 18 cell types, CD14 Mono pseudobulks are expected to be small (tens of cells or fewer) and some donor x condition groups may fall below the 10-cell threshold; verify this yourself by tabulating.
briefing.reason: Tells the team which columns and labels to use, that X is already raw counts, and warns that the pseudobulks will be small, which shapes every later modelling choice.

briefing.text: PITFALL - building the pseudobulk the wrong way. Averaging or summing normalized/log-transformed values instead of summing raw integer counts breaks the negative-binomial model. Testing cells as replicates (Wilcoxon/t-test on cells, or donor as a covariate in a cell-level model) is pseudoreplication: false positives are heavily inflated, almost every gene passes FDR, and a top 20 by LFC turns into a list of rare genes. CHECK: the aggregated matrix is integer-valued raw counts; there is one profile per donor x cytokine built from CD14 Mono cells only; the >=10-cell rule is applied to the number of CD14 Mono cells in that donor x cytokine, not to all cell types in the sample; the DE input has as many rows as pseudobulks, not cells; pseudobulk sums are integers. IF FOUND: rebuild by summing raw counts per donor x cytokine and run a bulk count model (DESeq2/PyDESeq2 or edgeR) with the donor as the replicate unit.
briefing.reason: A wrong aggregation or a cell-level test would invalidate the statistics and change the gene list; the >=10-cell rule is also easy to apply to the wrong cell set.

briefing.text: PITFALL - which samples enter the model. Fitting the DE model on all 91 cytokine conditions (up to 1092 pseudobulks) instead of only IFN-beta and PBS changes the answer: DESeq2 estimates one dispersion per gene and the size factors across every sample in the model, so unrelated cytokines with different variability shift the IFN-beta vs PBS p-values (a reported case showed only ~60% overlap of significant genes between the all-groups and two-group fits), and with ~1000 sparse pseudobulks almost no gene is non-zero in every sample, which breaks median-of-ratios size factors. CHECK: state how many pseudobulks and which cytokine levels enter the model; if all conditions were fitted, compare the top 20 against a fit restricted to IFN-beta + PBS. IF FOUND: for this two-condition question fit only the IFN-beta and PBS CD14 Mono pseudobulks with design ~ donor + condition. Do not use the obs column 'treatment' as the condition: it lumps all 90 cytokines together against PBS.
briefing.reason: The choice of samples in the fit and of the condition column directly changes p-values and the top-20 list; the 'treatment' column is a trap that would test the wrong comparison.

briefing.text: PITFALL - unpaired donors in a donor-blocked design. With design ~ donor + condition, a donor that has only one of the two conditions left after the >=10-cell filter contributes nothing to the IFN-beta vs PBS estimate, yet it still enters size-factor estimation, dispersion estimation and the baseMean used for independent filtering. Dropping the donor term instead throws away most of the power when donors differ. CHECK: after filtering pseudobulks to >=10 CD14 Mono cells, tabulate donor x condition (IFN-beta, PBS) with cell counts and total counts per pseudobulk; confirm how many donors have both; confirm the design matrix is full rank. IF FOUND: keep only donors that have both an IFN-beta and a PBS pseudobulk, keep donor as a fixed blocking factor (~ donor + condition), and report the number of pairs used; do not switch to an unpaired design to rescue unpaired donors.
briefing.reason: The task requires controlling for donor; how unpaired donors are handled after the cell-count filter affects normalization, dispersions and filtering, and so the result.

briefing.text: PITFALL - contrast direction and level names. Python/R choose the reference level alphabetically and 'IFN-beta' sorts before 'PBS', so a default coefficient is PBS vs IFN-beta and the genes that look 'upregulated' are really the repressed ones. PyDESeq2 needs contrast=['variable','tested_level','ref_level'], and the lfc_shrink coefficient name (format like 'condition[T.IFN-beta]' in recent versions) must match a fitted coefficient, which exists only if PBS is the reference. Hyphens, spaces and underscores in level or column names may be rewritten by the tool. CHECK: print the design-matrix columns / dds.varm['LFC'] column names and the results header stating the comparison ('IFN-beta vs PBS'); confirm that a few canonical interferon-stimulated genes have positive LFC and that normalized counts of the top genes are higher in IFN-beta samples in every donor. IF FOUND: set PBS as reference explicitly (ordered categorical or ref_level), pass the contrast explicitly as [factor, 'IFN-beta', 'PBS'], and rename levels to plain alphanumerics (e.g. IFNb, PBS) before fitting if the tool complains.
briefing.reason: A sign flip would report repressed genes as the induced ones; the default alphabetical reference makes this the likely outcome unless it is set explicitly.

briefing.text: PITFALL - size factors on sparse pseudobulks. Median-of-ratios size factors (DESeq2 default; PyDESeq2 size_factors_fit_type='ratio') use only genes with a non-zero count in every sample. Pseudobulks of 10-30 cells are sparse, so the size factors may rest on a few dozen very highly expressed genes (or fail with 'every gene contains at least one zero'); if those genes are themselves interferon-responsive, normalization absorbs part of the treatment effect and biases every LFC. CHECK: count genes with all-positive counts across the pseudobulks in the model; compare size factors with total counts per pseudobulk (should be roughly proportional) and with number of cells; look for a pseudobulk whose size factor is far from the rest. IF FOUND: remove low-count genes first, then use the 'poscounts' estimator or supply library-size/TMM-type size factors; never add a pseudocount of 1 to the count matrix to get around the error; consider dropping a pseudobulk whose library is an order of magnitude smaller than the others.
briefing.reason: Normalization on few-cell pseudobulks can fail or bias all fold changes, which changes a ranking that is based on log2FoldChange.

briefing.text: PITFALL - very small pseudobulks. Pseudobulks of 10-30 cells are well below what practitioners treat as reliable (workflow guides suggest about 50 cells per sample), and cell numbers and library sizes vary several-fold between donor x condition groups, so a few tiny pseudobulks can drive both the dispersion estimates and the largest fold changes. Interferon treatment may also change how many cells are labelled CD14 Mono, which would make IFN-beta pseudobulks systematically smaller than PBS ones. CHECK: tabulate cells and total counts per pseudobulk for IFN-beta and PBS by donor; look at the first principal components of the normalized pseudobulks to see whether a sample separates by size rather than by condition; repeat the DE with a stricter threshold (e.g. >=20 cells) and compare top-20 overlap. IF FOUND: keep the task's >=10-cell rule for the reported answer, but apply a firm gene-expression filter, flag genes whose rank depends on one small pseudobulk, and report how stable the top 20 is to the cell threshold.
briefing.reason: Tells the team to keep the task's stated threshold for the reported answer while testing whether the top 20 is driven by a few tiny samples.

briefing.text: PITFALL - ranking by raw log2FoldChange favours low-count genes. Ratios are noisiest at low counts: a gene with zeros in every PBS pseudobulk and a handful of reads in IFN-beta gets a huge maximum-likelihood LFC and can still pass FDR<0.05 across the donor pairs, pushing well-expressed induced genes out of the top 20. CHECK: for the top 20, print baseMean and the raw pseudobulk counts per sample in PBS and IFN-beta; count how many have near-zero PBS counts or baseMean below ~10; re-rank with apeglm-shrunken LFC (lfcShrink / PyDESeq2 lfc_shrink) and with a pre-fit expression filter, and report the overlap of the three top-20 lists. IF FOUND: apply an explicit gene-expression filter before fitting (e.g. >=10 counts in at least as many samples as the smaller group, or edgeR filterByExpr / decoupler filter_by_expr) and state whether the ranking uses MLE or shrunken LFC. Shrinkage changes only the LFC, not the Wald p-values/padj, so the FDR<0.05 set is the same and only the order changes. The task wording ('log2FoldChange', 'FDR') follows DESeq2 column names, so keep the MLE-ranked list available as well as the shrunken one and say which one is reported.
briefing.reason: The answer is defined as the top 20 by log2FoldChange, so how low-count genes are filtered and whether LFC is shrunken decides which genes make the list; the team must choose this deliberately and state it.

briefing.text: PITFALL - independent filtering, alpha and NaN padj. DESeq2-style results set padj to NA for genes below an automatically chosen mean-count threshold (PyDESeq2: independent_filter=True, alpha=0.05 by default; R DESeq2 default alpha is 0.1), and a comparison such as padj<0.05 silently drops NaN rows. Pre-filtering genes changes the multiple-testing universe, and a mismatch between the alpha used for filtering and the 0.05 cut-off gives a slightly different significant set. CHECK: report the number of genes tested, with NaN padj, and with padj<0.05 and LFC>0; confirm alpha=0.05 was used in the results call; confirm NaN-padj genes are excluded on purpose rather than treated as significant or as zero; vary the pre-filter (none, >=10 counts in >=n samples, filter_by_expr) and see whether the top 20 moves. IF FOUND: fix alpha=0.05, filter genes once per cell type before fitting (single-cell best practice is to remove lowly expressed genes per cell type), and report the filter used alongside the list.
briefing.reason: Which genes are eligible at FDR<0.05 depends on these settings, and the eligible set is what gets ranked for the top 20.

briefing.text: PITFALL - Cook's-distance outlier handling can remove genuinely induced genes. PyDESeq2 defaults are refit_cooks=True with min_replicates=7 and cooks_filter=True: with >=7 replicates per condition an 'outlier' count is replaced by a trimmed mean; with fewer, the gene's p-value is set to NA. In small pseudobulks a strongly induced gene whose response is uneven across donors looks like an outlier, so it can vanish from an FDR<0.05 list or get a reduced fold change. CHECK: count genes with NaN pvalue (distinct from NaN padj) and genes with replaced counts; list those with large positive LFC; rerun with refit_cooks=False and cooks_filter=False (R: minReplicatesForReplace=Inf, cooksCutoff=FALSE) and compare the top 20. IF FOUND: inspect the per-sample counts of the affected genes; if a gene is consistently higher in IFN-beta across donors, treat the flag as a false alarm and report results with outlier handling disabled, saying so.
briefing.reason: Strongly induced genes are exactly the ones the task asks for and the ones most likely to be flagged or altered by default outlier handling, so this can change the top 20.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team observed that the IFN-beta pseudobulks have size factors several-fold smaller than the PBS ones, and concluded that a rule of the form 'at least N raw counts in at least K samples' is much harder to meet in IFN-beta samples than in PBS samples, so it works against genes that are expressed mainly after treatment. Your rule needs 7 samples and you have exactly 7 IFN-beta samples, so a gene that is near zero in PBS must reach the raw threshold in every one of the small IFN-beta pseudobulks. Check in your data: how many genes that are significant and up under a weaker, condition-agnostic filter are removed by your rule; for the removed ones, look at raw and normalized counts per donor and say whether they are supported across donors or by one or two samples; and check whether a depth-aware version of your rule (same idea on counts-per-million or normalized counts rather than raw counts) keeps the same genes. Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the two teams did not put the same samples in the model. The task's step 2 says to create pseudobulks by donor x cytokine with at least 10 cells and says nothing about dropping donors that lack one condition. The other team fitted every IFN-beta and PBS pseudobulk that passes the cell threshold, including PBS pseudobulks from donors with no qualifying IFN-beta sample, and compared that with a paired-only fit. Check in your implementation what changes when the unpaired PBS pseudobulks are included: the genes passing your filter, the size factors, the dispersion trend, baseMean and the independent-filtering threshold, and the top 20. Which reading of the task do the task's own words support? Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: both teams wrote their own DESeq2-style fit, and the two implementations do not describe the same multiple-testing step: you apply independent filtering before BH, the other team's notes describe BH alone. Report, for your fit: the mean-count threshold your independent filtering chose and how it was chosen, how many significant up genes it removes or adds compared with plain BH on the same genes, and whether the top 20 moves. Also report how your GLM estimates log2FoldChange for a gene with zero counts in every PBS pseudobulk (is the estimate bounded, penalised, or allowed to run to the iteration limit?), since the ranking is decided there. Can you test your implementation on a small input where the reference result is known or derivable? Does any of this change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your plan said that a top list dominated by low-count genes would lead you to a stronger expression filter. You then recorded top genes with baseMean around 1-3 and moved to a weaker filter instead. The other team found that with a weak or absent filter low-count genes enter the top of the list, and it accepted a top-20 gene only after printing its normalized counts per donor in both conditions and seeing it raised in every paired donor. Check each gene in your top 20: raw and normalized counts per pseudobulk, in how many of the IFN-beta pseudobulks it is non-zero, in how many paired donors it rises, and whether the fold change rests on one or two samples. Is 'biased against treatment-only genes' or 'low-count noise' the better description of the genes your filter change let in? Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team's DESeq2-style fit applies independent filtering on mean normalized count at alpha 0.05 before BH, as the reference tool's results step does by default; your notes describe BH alone. It also re-ranked its significant genes by shrunken fold change, and repeated the analysis leaving out each of the two donors that have exactly 10 IFN-beta cells. None of these appear in your checks. In your data: how many of your top 20 would lose their adjusted p-value under independent filtering, how much of your top 20 survives a shrunken-fold-change ranking, and how much survives leaving out each 10-cell donor? Also report how your GLM estimates log2FoldChange for a gene with zero counts in every PBS pseudobulk (bounded, penalised, or run to the iteration limit?). Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your plan and your first warning sign both said to keep only donors with both conditions, but your final fit used all PBS pseudobulks, including those from donors with no qualifying IFN-beta sample; the other team fitted paired donors only. You report the top 20 is the same either way. Check whether that holds under every gene filter you tried and not only one, and whether the row-sum filter itself changes when the sum runs over the paired pseudobulks only (the unpaired PBS samples are the deep ones and add counts to the row sum without informing the contrast). Compare size factors, the dispersion trend and baseMean between the two sample sets. Why did the final fit depart from your plan, and does this change your method?

In standard pseudobulk differential-expression workflows built on DESeq2/PyDESeq2 or edgeR, what low-expression gene filter is applied by default before fitting, with exact default parameter values (edgeR filterByExpr and decoupler's filter_by_expr: min_count, min_total_count, large_n, min_prop; the DESeq2 vignette's recommended pre-filter and its 'smallest group size' variant)? How does each rule account for samples with very different library sizes and for the size of the smallest group?
questions.why: The two teams' lists differ mainly because one used a per-sample raw-count rule and the other a row-sum rule; knowing which rule the reference workflows actually apply, and whether it is depth-aware, would let both teams judge their filter against a convention rather than against their own results.

questions.question: For a gene with zero counts in every sample of the reference condition and non-zero counts in the treated condition, what maximum-likelihood log2FoldChange do DESeq2 and PyDESeq2 report under default settings (coefficient bounds, ridge penalty in the IRLS step, fallback optimizer when IRLS does not converge), and is that gene's Wald p-value and adjusted p-value kept or set to NA?
questions.why: Both teams used hand-written NB GLMs and rank by unshrunken fold change, so the top of the list is decided by exactly these near-zero-baseline genes; if the reference tools bound or penalise such estimates differently from the custom fits, the ranking differs.

questions.question: How exactly do DESeq2 and PyDESeq2 choose the mean-normalized-count threshold in independent filtering (the grid of quantiles, the lowess fit of rejections against quantile, and the rule for picking the threshold), and with a paired design of about seven samples per condition and no replicates within a donor-by-condition cell, do Cook's-distance outlier filtering and count replacement apply by default?
questions.why: One team applied independent filtering and the other did not, and both skipped Cook's handling; the exact default behaviour determines which low-count genes can reach FDR<0.05 and therefore enter a top-20 ranked by fold change.

findings.question: In standard pseudobulk differential-expression workflows built on DESeq2/PyDESeq2 or edgeR, what low-expression gene filter is applied by default before fitting, with exact default parameter values (edgeR filterByExpr and decoupler's filter_by_expr: min_count, min_total_count, large_n, min_prop; the DESeq2 vignette's recommended pre-filter and its 'smallest group size' variant)? How does each rule account for samples with very different library sizes and for the size of the smallest group?
findings.answer: edgeR filterByExpr and decoupler filter_by_expr use the same defaults: min_count=10, min_total_count=15, large_n=10, min_prop=0.7. decoupler says it is adapted from edgeR. The edgeR source shows the rule is depth-aware. CPM cutoff = min_count / median(library size) * 1e6, and a gene is kept if CPM >= cutoff in at least n samples AND its total raw count across samples >= 15. A sample with a small library therefore needs fewer raw reads to count as expressing the gene. How n is set: (1) If group is given, n is the smallest group size. (2) If a design is given and no group, n = 1/max(hat value); for a balanced ~donor+condition design with 7 pairs this is 14/8 = 1.75, so effectively 2 samples. (3) With neither, which is decoupler's default group=None, all samples count as one group, so n = the number of samples. If n > large_n, it is relaxed to 10 + (n-10)*0.7; for 14 samples that is 12.8. The DESeq2 vignette's pre-filter is keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= smallestGroupSize: a raw count of at least 10 in at least as many samples as the smallest group (7 for 7 vs 7). Without discrete groups it uses the minimal number of samples where non-zero counts would be interesting. This rule works on raw counts, so it is not depth-aware. The vignette calls it optional, since results() runs independent filtering anyway. A plain row-sum filter is not the default of any of these tools.

findings.question: For a gene with zero counts in every sample of the reference condition and non-zero counts in the treated condition, what maximum-likelihood log2FoldChange do DESeq2 and PyDESeq2 report under default settings (coefficient bounds, ridge penalty in the IRLS step, fallback optimizer when IRLS does not converge), and is that gene's Wald p-value and adjusted p-value kept or set to NA?
findings.answer: Both tools report a finite but bounded MLE, and the bounds differ between them. R DESeq2 (betaPrior=FALSE): the ridge is lambda=1e-6 per coefficient on the log2 scale, passed to IRLS as lambda/log(2)^2, with betaTol=1e-8 and maxit=100. Rows that do not converge, are unstable (NA betas) or have non-positive variance are refit by optim L-BFGS-B with bounds lower=-30, upper=30 on the LOG2 scale. A NEWS snippet, which I did not open as a full page, says rows with |beta|>=30 also take this path. PyDESeq2 irls_solver: ridge_factor=1e-6 on the natural-log scale, maxiter=250, min_beta=-30 and max_beta=30 on the NATURAL-LOG scale. If any |beta| > 30 or maxiter is reached, it switches to L-BFGS-B bounded to [-30, 30] natural log, about +-43.3 in log2. If that fails and there are <=2 variables, it uses grid search. log2FoldChange is reported as beta/ln(2). min_mu is 0.5 in both. So for zero-baseline genes the reported LFC is large, sits near or on the bounds, depends on the optimizer, and can differ between R and Python. P-values: neither tool sets a gene's p-value to NA because the reference group is all zero. In R, only rows that are zero in every sample get NA for LFC, p and padj. Otherwise p is set to NA only for Cook's outliers, and padj only by independent filtering for low baseMean. PyDESeq2 likewise keeps the Wald p-value. The web did not settle whether such genes actually reach padj<0.05; that depends on their fitted SE.
findings.confidence: high for bounds/ridge/optimizer and NA rules; low on whether such genes are significant

findings.question: How exactly do DESeq2 and PyDESeq2 choose the mean-normalized-count threshold in independent filtering (the grid of quantiles, the lowess fit of rejections against quantile, and the rule for picking the threshold), and with a paired design of about seven samples per condition and no replicates within a donor-by-condition cell, do Cook's-distance outlier filtering and count replacement apply by default?
findings.answer: Independent filtering is the same in both tools. The filter is baseMean. theta = 50 equally spaced quantiles from lowerQuantile = fraction of genes with baseMean==0 up to 0.95, or up to 1 if lowerQuantile >= 0.95. For each quantile cutoff, BH is applied to genes with baseMean >= cutoff and a non-NA p-value, and rejections are counted at padj < alpha. alpha defaults to 0.1 in R results() and 0.05 in PyDESeq2. A lowess curve (f=1/5) is fitted to the rejections against theta. If max rejections <= 10, the first theta is used, which means no filtering. Otherwise thresh = max(lowess fit) - RMSE of the residuals (only where rejections > 0), and the threshold is the first theta whose rejections exceed thresh. R falls back to 90% and then 80% of the max fit before using the first theta; PyDESeq2 goes straight to the first theta. Genes below the chosen cutoff get padj=NA; their p-values are kept. Cook's handling: flagging uses only samples whose design-matrix row occurs >= 3 times. R's vignette says flagging needs 3 or more replicates; PyDESeq2 uses n_or_more_replicates(design_matrix, 3), noted in its code as 'As in DESeq2'. The cutoff is the F(0.99; p, m-p) quantile. Replacement requires >= 7 samples sharing an identical design-matrix row (minReplicatesForReplace=7, nOrMoreInCell on the model matrix; PyDESeq2 min_replicates=7). With ~donor+condition and one sample per donor-by-condition cell, every design row is unique. So by default no gene is flagged as a Cook's outlier and no counts are replaced, and skipping Cook's handling changes nothing for this design. One caveat: I confirmed the R side of the >=3 rule from the vignette and the PyDESeq2 code comment, not from R's recordMaxCooks source.

R's vignette says flagging needs 3 or more replicates; PyDESeq2 uses n_or_more_replicates(design_matrix, 3), noted in its code as 'As in DESeq2'. The cutoff is the F(0.99; p, m-p) quantile. Replacement requires >= 7 samples sharing an identical design-matrix row (minReplicatesForReplace=7, nOrMoreInCell on the model matrix; PyDESeq2 min_replicates=7). With ~donor+condition and one sample per donor-by-condition cell, every design row is unique. So by default no gene is flagged as a Cook's outlier and no counts are replaced, and skipping Cook's handling changes nothing for this design. One caveat: I confirmed the R side of the >=3 rule from the vignette and the PyDESeq2 code comment, not from R's recordMaxCooks source. HOW SURE: high.
